- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use moving average of last 5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is rising.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.2 → 0.8), model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment momentum.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day for next 5 days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly positive.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.2–0.8), model overfits short-term noise; use 3-day moving average of true values to anchor forecast.
